jobs.title: Program Coordinator
Community Engagement Program Manager (ALUMNI EXTERNAL REL SPEC 3)
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Community Engagement Program Manager for the UC Davis Arboretum and Public Garden (APG) will develop and implement specialized programs, events, and communications designed to inform and engage key constituencies. Key APG constituencies include the general public, community volunteers, pipeline donors, students, and other campus and community partners and representatives. This position will work closely with the Arboretum and Public Garden Director and Assistant Director of Development in implementing partnerships and programs to help grow support of the Arboretum and Public Garden.

Apply By Date

7/20/2026 by 11:59 pm

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications - For full consideration, applicants are encouraged to upload license and/or certification if required of the position

Bachelors Degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Experience planning and implementing community engagement programs and events. Ability to support and enhance community relations.
Experience creating positive working relationships with adult volunteers including recruiting, training, identifying engaging roles and projects, and recognizing accomplishments.
Thorough written, verbal and interpersonal communications, tact and political acumen to effectively represent the Arboretum and Public Garden and UC Davis, including in highly sensitive situations.
Thorough research, analytical and critical thinking skills, including sound judgment and decision-making skills. Problem-solving skills to correctly identify real and potential issues, advising management as required, and proposing effective strategic solutions.
Organizational and project management skills, including program/event planning and meeting deadlines.
Demonstrated ability to lead by example, fostering teamwork and an open culture focused on service, innovation, and collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting fundraising activities including relationship building, donor stewardship, events, and communications.
Experience with supporting earned-income activities such as membership programs, dedication programs and/or merchandise sales.
Experience working with and fostering leadership in young people (e.g., college students).
Experience working with a volunteer board or other group of leadership volunteers.
Knowledge of the university environment and ability to work effectively with other campus units. Knowledge of museums and informal learning environments.
Knowledge of Arboretum and Public Garden mission, horticultural programs, plant collections, volunteer opportunities and practices.
Ability to initiate new strategies, partnerships, and approaches.

Key Responsibilities

75% - Community Engagement, Membership, and Volunteer Program Management
25% - Community Engagement Communications

Department Overview

The UC Davis Arboretum and Public Garden (APG) holds responsibility for managing the entire campus landscape. = The goals of the APG are to create a more visitor-friendly campus, transition to a more sustainable and resilient campus landscape that is adapted to our future climate, make the academic programs of UC Davis visible to campus visitors, build environmental leadership in students and community partners, engage the public in lifelong learning opportunities, and leverage campus financial and human resources.

Key programs of the APG include the UC Davis GATEways Project, the Learning by Leading™ Program, and the Living Landscape Adaptation Plan. The GATEways Project transforms the campus into physical and programmatic portals for the public to engage in the riches of UC Davis. The Learning by Leading Program builds environmental leadership skills with students through hands-on, real-world projects and programs involving mentorship by staff, faculty and community members. The Living Landscape Adaptation Plan charts a course for sustaining a thriving campus landscape in the face of significant climate change disruptions.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator (MARKETING SPEC 2 CM)
jobs.description:
Job Summary

Under the direction of the Faculty Director of the UC Davis Olive Center, this position supports the development and coordination of industry engagement, extension activities, and experiential education programs related to olive production and processing in California. The position assists with stakeholder engagement, educational outreach, product marketing, and implementation of extension and research activities aligned with the Center’s mission.

The position also supports implementation of OLEA 360, an immersive educational and workforce development program focused on olive growing, milling, quality evaluation, and product development. Responsibilities include coordinating activities with the Student Farm, local growers, processors, and industry partners; assisting with educational programming and outreach; and supporting program logistics, communication, and industry engagement activities throughout the year.

Apply By Date

07/20/2026 by 11:59 pm

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications - For full consideration, applicants are encouraged to upload license and/or certification if required of the position

Bachelor’s degree in agriculture, plant sciences, food science, agricultural education, environmental sciences, sustainable agriculture, agricultural business, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience/training.
Minimum 1–2 years of experience in agricultural extension, grower outreach, program coordination, educational program support, marketing, communications or related field experience.
Experience working effectively with agricultural producers, students, community stakeholders, or industry partners.
Strong organizational and project coordination skills with the ability to manage multiple activities and timelines simultaneously.
Effective interpersonal and communication skills to work collaboratively with growers, industry partners, students, faculty, and community stakeholders.
Ability to coordinate outreach, educational, and stakeholder engagement activities with professionalism and attention to detail.
Knowledge of basic agricultural production systems, extension programming, or applied educational activities.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with olive production, specialty crops, sustainable agriculture, or food and agricultural systems.
Experience supporting experiential learning, workforce development, or educational outreach programs.
Experience coordinating field-based activities, workshops, or applied extension programs.
Experience working in university, nonprofit, agricultural, or research environments.
Experience with stakeholder communication, partnership development, and program logistics coordination.
Knowledge of olive production systems, olive oil processing, or specialty crop agriculture.
Familiarity with extension, outreach, or experiential learning programs within higher education or agricultural settings
Familiarity with product marketing, promotional campaigns, branding, or product launches.
Familiarity with student engagement or workforce development programs.

Key Responsibilities

40% - Extension, Industry Engagement, and OLEA 360 Coordination
30% - Olive Center Product Marketing and Sales Support
15% - Extension, Education, and Research Support
15% - Special Project

Department Overview

The UC Davis Olive Center is a research, education, and outreach center within the University of California, Davis is dedicated to advancing the quality, sustainability, and economic viability of the olive industry through independent, science-based research and extension. The Center works closely with growers, processors, researchers, students, and industry stakeholders to support innovation in olive production, processing, quality assurance, workforce development, and consumer education.

The Olive Center develops and delivers applied research, extension programs, short courses, industry outreach activities, and experiential learning opportunities that benefit California agriculture and food systems. The Center also serves as a trusted source of technical expertise and educational resources for the olive oil industry and broader public.
